Set category_id to null for all products in this category (making them uncategorized).

Set deleted_at to current timestamp on the target category record (soft delete).

Return success without response body.

Handle edge cases:
- Category not found: return 404 error
- Already deleted: return 409 conflict error
- Not administrator: return 403 forbidden error
- Database constraint violations: return 500 error with appropriate message
operations.description:
Delete a category from the shopping mall platform. This operation is exclusively available to administrators.

When a category is deleted, the system performs a soft deletion by setting the deleted_at timestamp, which removes the category from all active listings while preserving the data for audit purposes. All products that were assigned to the deleted category are automatically moved to an uncategorized state (their category_id is set to null), ensuring no product data is lost.

If the deleted category has subcategories, those subcategories are also soft deleted as part of the cascade operation. This maintains the integrity of the category hierarchy and prevents orphaned subcategories from remaining in the system.

Only users with administrator privileges (regular or super administrator grade) can perform this operation. Customer and seller accounts are explicitly denied access to category management functions. The system logs all deletion attempts for security and audit trail purposes.

Related operations include GET /categories to list all active categories, POST /admin/categories to create new categories, and PUT /admin/categories/{categoryId} to update existing category information.

parameters.name: categoryId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the category to delete (global scope)

operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_orders table with pagination and filtering support.

1. Parse request body for search criteria:
   - status filter (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded, partially_completed)
   - date range filters (created_at start and end)
   - price range filters (total_price min and max)
   - pagination parameters (page, limit, sort field, sort direction)

2. Apply role-based filtering:
   - For customers: filter by shopping_mall_customer_id = current user's customer ID
   - For sellers: join with shopping_mall_order_items, filter by shopping_mall_seller_id = current user's seller ID
   - For admins: no additional filtering, return all orders

3. Execute query with ORDER BY created_at DESC (newest first by default)

4. Apply cursor-based or offset-based pagination based on limit parameter

5. Return paginated response with order summaries including:
   - Order ID, status, total_price, created_at
   - Shipping address snapshot (read-only)
   - Order item count
   - Customer display name

6. Handle soft-deleted orders by excluding records where deleted_at is not null

7. Implement idempotency for read operations - same query parameters should return consistent results
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of shopping mall orders based on search criteria.

This operation provides comprehensive order listing capabilities with support for filtering by order status, date ranges, price ranges, and sorting preferences. The response includes order summaries optimized for list displays, containing essential information such as order ID, status, total price, creation timestamp, and shipping address snapshot.

The shipping address is stored as an immutable snapshot at the time of order placement, ensuring historical accuracy even if the customer later modifies or deletes their address. This preserves the exact delivery location used for each order, which is critical for order fulfillment, dispute resolution, and order history accuracy.

Authorization is role-based: customers can only view their own orders, sellers can view orders containing their products, and administrators can view all platform orders. The operation supports flexible pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting options to efficiently handle large order datasets.

Related operations include GET /orders/{orderId} for retrieving detailed order information, POST /orders for creating new orders, and various order item operations for cancellations, refunds, and shipments.

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for order listing

responseBody.description: Paginated list of order summaries

operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_orders table by id and shopping_mall_customer_id (from authenticated user's JWT token) to enforce data isolation.

Join with shopping_mall_order_items on order.id = order_item.shopping_mall_order_id to retrieve all line items.

For each order item, include:
- Product snapshot (product_snapshot field) - contains product name, description at purchase time
- Variant snapshot (variant_snapshot field) - contains SKU, option values at purchase time
- Seller profile snapshot (seller_profile_snapshot field) - contains shop name at purchase time
- Quantity, price, and current status

Include shipping_address_snapshot from the order record (JSON string containing address details at purchase time).

Include order-level status which is derived from all order item statuses.

Return 404 if order not found or if authenticated customer does not own the order.

Return 403 if customer account is banned (check customer account state).

Support soft-deleted orders: exclude orders where deleted_at is not null.
operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information for a specific customer order including all order items, shipping address, and order status.

This operation provides complete order details for a customer's purchase transaction. The response includes the order header information (total price, overall status, creation date) and all line items within the order. Each order item contains the product snapshot, variant snapshot, and seller profile snapshot as they existed at the time of purchase, ensuring historical accuracy even if products or seller profiles are later modified or deleted.

The shipping address is returned as a snapshot captured at checkout time, preserving the exact delivery location used for fulfillment. This address remains immutable and is not affected by any subsequent changes to the customer's address book.

Access is restricted to the order's owner only. The authenticated customer can only view their own orders, enforcing data isolation between customers. Orders from deleted customer accounts remain accessible for seller and legal record purposes, but banned customers cannot access their order history.

This endpoint is typically used after retrieving the order list from GET /customers/me/orders to view full details of a specific order, including shipment tracking information and the ability to request cancellations or refunds for eligible items.

parameters.name: orderId
parameters.description: UUID of the order to retrieve

responseBody.description: Detailed order information with all order items

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of order items within a specific customer order.

This operation provides access to individual line items that comprise a customer's order transaction. Each order item represents a purchased product with its quantity, price at time of purchase, and current fulfillment status. The order items are stored in the shopping_mall_order_items table with relationships to the parent order, selling merchant, and various fulfillment entities.

Order items maintain independent status tracking (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded) even within the same order, allowing different items to be fulfilled at different times. Purchase-time snapshots (product_snapshot, variant_snapshot, seller_profile_snapshot) preserve the exact state of referenced entities at order placement time, ensuring order history remains accurate even if products or seller profiles are later modified or deleted.

Security: Only authenticated customers can access order items from their own orders. The system validates that the requesting customer owns the specified order before returning any items. Sellers can only view order items containing their products through the seller-specific endpoint. Administrators have access to all order items across the platform.

Related operations: GET /orders/{orderId} retrieves the parent order summary. POST /orders/{orderId}/items/{itemId}/cancel requests cancellation of a specific item. POST /orders/{orderId}/items/{itemId}/refund requests a refund for a delivered item. GET /products/{productId}/reviews retrieves reviews for products in the order.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_order_items table filtering by shopping_mall_order_id path parameter. Apply additional filters from request body (status, seller_id, search terms). Implement cursor-based pagination for large result sets with configurable page size.

Authorization: Validate that the authenticated customer's ID matches the shopping_mall_customer_id of the referenced order in shopping_mall_orders table. Deny access if customer doesn't own the order.

Database query: SELECT order items WHERE shopping_mall_order_id = {orderId} AND deleted_at IS NULL, with additional WHERE clauses for status and other filters. JOIN with shopping_mall_orders to verify customer ownership.

Response transformation: Map order items to IShoppingMallOrderItem.ISummary format, including id, quantity, price, status, product_snapshot (parsed JSON), variant_snapshot (parsed JSON), and created_at. Exclude seller_profile_snapshot from summary for performance.

Pagination: Support page and limit parameters with default page=1, limit=20, max limit=100. Calculate total count for pagination metadata. Return IPageIShoppingMallOrderItem.ISummary with pagination object and data array.

Error handling: Return 404 if order not found. Return 403 if customer doesn't own order. Return 400 for invalid filter parameters or pagination values.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of order item summaries within the specified order

parameters.description: Target order's UUID identifier
parameters.name: orderId

requestBody.description: Search filters and pagination parameters for order items

prerequisites.description: Order must be created before order items can be retrieved

operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the shopping_mall_order_items table for the item matching both orderId and itemId parameters.

Authorization validation:
- For customer requests: Verify the order belongs to the authenticated customer by checking shopping_mall_customer_id matches the customer's ID
- For seller requests: Verify the item belongs to the seller by checking shopping_mall_seller_id matches the seller's ID
- For admin requests: Allow access to all order items

Query execution:
1. Fetch the order item record by id = itemId and shopping_mall_order_id = orderId
2. Verify the item exists and is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is NULL)
3. Join with shopping_mall_shipments to retrieve any associated shipment records (tracking carrier, tracking number, shipped at, delivered at, delivery confirmed status)
4. Parse the JSON snapshot fields (product_snapshot, variant_snapshot, seller_profile_snapshot) for structured data access

Business logic:
- Return 404 if order item not found or if authorization fails
- Return 403 if user attempts to access another user's order item
- Include shipment information in response if the item has been shipped (status = 'shipped' or 'delivered')
- Ensure order item status is included: paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded

Error handling:
- Return appropriate error codes for unauthorized access, not found, or invalid parameters
- Log access attempts for audit purposes
operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific order item within a customer order.

This operation returns comprehensive details about a single order line item, including the quantity purchased, unit price at time of purchase, current fulfillment status, and complete snapshots of the product, product variant, and seller profile as they existed when the order was placed. The order item status indicates its current state in the fulfillment workflow: paid (order confirmed), shipped (item dispatched), delivered (item received), cancelled (pre-shipment cancellation approved), or refunded (post-delivery return approved).

Security and authorization are strictly enforced. Customers can only access order items from their own orders. Sellers can only view order items containing their products. Administrators have access to all order items across the platform. This ensures proper data isolation and prevents unauthorized access to purchase information.

The response includes associated shipment information when available, such as tracking carrier name, tracking number, shipment date, delivery confirmation status, and actual delivery timestamp. This enables customers to track their purchases and sellers to manage their fulfillment operations effectively.

Related operations include GET /orders/{orderId} for viewing the complete order with all items, GET /customers/me/orders for listing all customer orders, and GET /sellers/me/orders for sellers to view their order items. For shipment-specific actions, use POST /sellers/me/shipments to create shipments and POST /customers/me/shipments/{shipmentId}/confirm-delivery to confirm delivery.

parameters.name: orderId
parameters.description: UUID of the parent order containing this order item

parameters.name: itemId
parameters.description: UUID of the specific order item to retrieve

responseBody.description: Complete order item details including product snapshots, seller information, and shipment data

operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_wishlist_items table for the authenticated customer's wishlist items.

1. Extract customer ID from JWT authentication token
2. Apply soft-delete filter (deleted_at IS NULL)
3. Apply optional filters from request body:
   - product_status: filter by product availability (in_stock, out_of_stock, deleted)
   - created_after/created_before: date range filtering
   - sort_by: 'created_at' (default), 'updated_at'
   - sort_order: 'asc', 'desc' (default 'desc' for newest first)
4. Apply pagination: page, limit (default 20, max 100)
5. Join with products table to include product summary information
6. Join with shopping_mall_customers to verify ownership
7. Return paginated results with product details

Error handling:
- Return 401 if customer not authenticated
- Return 400 for invalid filter parameters
- Handle soft-deleted products gracefully (include with deleted status)
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of products in the authenticated customer's wishlist.

This operation allows customers to view their saved products with advanced filtering capabilities. The wishlist contains products that customers have bookmarked for future purchase consideration. Each wishlist item includes product information such as name, price, images, and availability status.

The response includes paginated results with product summaries optimized for list displays. Customers can filter their wishlist by product availability status (in stock, out of stock, or deleted products) and sort items by addition date or last update time.

Security: Only authenticated customers can access their own wishlist. The system enforces strict ownership validation to prevent cross-customer wishlist access. Wishlist items for deleted products are soft-deleted but remain visible with a deleted status indicator.

Related operations include POST /wishlist/{productId} to add products to the wishlist and DELETE /wishlist/{productId} to remove items. Customers can also view detailed product information using GET /products/{productId}.

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for wishlist items

responseBody.description: Paginated list of wishlist item summaries with product information

operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_wishlist_items table by ID with soft-delete filter (deleted_at IS NULL).

Verify ownership: Compare the authenticated customer's ID with the wishlist item's shopping_mall_customer_id. Return 403 Forbidden if they don't match.

Join with shopping_mall_products table on product_id to retrieve product details (name, description, base_price, main image).

Join with shopping_mall_sellers table to get seller profile information (shop_name, shop_description).

Calculate average rating by aggregating shopping_mall_reviews table for the product (average of rating field, count of reviews).

Check product stock status by joining with shopping_mall_product_variants and checking stock_quantity > 0.

Return 404 Not Found if wishlist item doesn't exist or is soft-deleted.

Return 403 Forbidden if customer doesn't own the wishlist item.

Ensure all joins handle NULL cases gracefully for optional data.
operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific wishlist item for the authenticated customer.

This operation returns comprehensive details about a single product saved in the customer's wishlist, including the product's main image, name, description, base price, seller information, and customer reviews. The wishlist item must belong to the authenticated customer - cross-customer access is strictly prohibited per privacy requirements.

The response includes product availability status (in stock or out of stock), average customer rating if reviews exist, and the seller's shop name. This enables customers to review their saved products and make informed purchasing decisions directly from the wishlist interface.

Security: Only the owning customer can access their wishlist items. The system verifies ownership by comparing the authenticated customer's ID with the wishlist item's customer reference. Unauthorized access attempts return a 403 Forbidden error.

Related operations: Use PATCH /wishlist to view the paginated list of all wishlist items, POST /wishlist/{productId} to add products, and DELETE /wishlist/{productId} to remove items.

parameters.name: wishlistItemId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the wishlist item to retrieve

responseBody.description: Detailed wishlist item with complete product and seller information

prerequisites.description: Wishlist item must be created before it can be retrieved. The POST operation adds a product to the customer's wishlist, creating the wishlist item record that this GET operation retrieves.

operations.description:
Add a product to the authenticated customer's wishlist.

This operation creates a new wishlist item that links the currently authenticated customer to a specific product, allowing the customer to bookmark products of interest for future purchase consideration. The wishlist item records the timestamp when the product was added and remains in the wishlist until the customer explicitly removes it or the product is deleted by the seller.

Security and authorization: Only authenticated customers can add products to their wishlist. The operation uses the customer's identity from the authentication session to associate the wishlist item with the correct account. Each customer's wishlist is private and isolated - customers can only view and modify their own wishlist items.

Validation rules: The product must exist and not be deleted. The system prevents duplicate wishlist entries - if the customer has already added this product to their wishlist, the operation will reject the request without creating a duplicate. The wishlist is maintained at the product level, not at the variant level, so customers add products to their wishlist without selecting specific variants.

Related operations: After adding a product to the wishlist, customers can view their wishlist using GET /wishlist, remove items using DELETE /wishlist/{productId}, or add products directly to their cart from the wishlist for purchase.
operations.name: create
operations.specification: Query the authentication context to obtain the current customer's ID. Validate that the customer is authenticated and has an active account status. Query the shopping_mall_products table to verify the product exists and is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null). Check for existing wishlist items in shopping_mall_wishlist_items where shopping_mall_customer_id equals the current customer's ID and the product matches, ensuring no duplicate exists. If validation passes, create a new record in shopping_mall_wishlist_items with the customer ID, product ID, and current timestamp for created_at and updated_at fields. Return the created wishlist item with all fields including id, shopping_mall_customer_id, product reference, created_at, and updated_at.

responseBody.description: The created wishlist item with product details

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the product to add to the wishlist
parameters.name: productId

operations.description:
Remove a product from the authenticated customer's wishlist.

This operation deletes a wishlist item from the customer's saved products collection. When a customer removes a product from their wishlist, the system permanently deletes the wishlist item record from the shopping_mall_wishlist_items table, immediately updating the customer's wishlist view to reflect the removal.

The operation requires customer authentication. Only the customer who owns the wishlist item can remove it. The system validates that the wishlist item exists and belongs to the requesting customer before performing the deletion. If the product is not in the customer's wishlist, the request is rejected.

After removal, the product itself remains available for all customers to browse and purchase. The customer can add the same product back to their wishlist at any time. No snapshot is created when a wishlist item is removed, as specified in the business rules.

Related operations include GET /wishlist to view the current wishlist, and POST /wishlist/{productId} to add a product to the wishlist.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Query the shopping_mall_wishlist_items table to find the wishlist item where shopping_mall_customer_id matches the authenticated customer's ID from the JWT token and the product reference matches the provided productId parameter.

Validate that the wishlist item exists and belongs to the requesting customer. If no matching record is found, return a 404 Not Found error.

Permanently delete the wishlist item record from the database. Do not use soft delete (do not set deleted_at), as the business requirement specifies permanent deletion.

Return 204 No Content on successful deletion.

Handle edge cases: If the product has been deleted by the seller, still allow removal from wishlist. If the customer is not authenticated, return 401 Unauthorized.

parameters.description: Product ID to remove from the customer's wishlist
parameters.name: productId

operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the shopping_mall_wishlist_item_snapshots table with pagination and filtering support.

1. Parse request body for pagination (page, limit), sorting (sortBy, sortOrder), and optional filters
2. Apply filters on:
   - shopping_mall_wishlist_item_id (specific wishlist item)
   - created_at range (date range filter)
3. Apply sorting on supported fields: created_at (default), id
4. Execute paginated query with offset/limit calculation
5. Return paginated response with snapshot summaries

Authorization: Only authenticated customers can view their own wishlist snapshots. Admins can view all snapshots.

Error handling:
- Return 401 if not authenticated
- Return 403 if customer tries to access other users' snapshots
- Return 400 for invalid pagination parameters
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of wishlist item snapshots for audit and historical reference.

This operation provides access to immutable snapshots of wishlist items that were captured at specific points in time. These snapshots preserve the complete state of wishlist items including customer reference, product reference, and creation timestamp. The snapshots are created automatically when wishlist items are modified and serve as an audit trail for data integrity and historical tracking.

Customers can view snapshots of their own wishlist items to understand the history of their saved products. The system automatically filters snapshots to only include those belonging to the authenticated customer's wishlist items. Administrators have access to view all wishlist item snapshots across the platform for compliance and dispute resolution purposes.

The response includes pagination metadata (total count, current page, page size) and an array of snapshot summaries. Each snapshot contains the immutable snapshot data captured at creation time, along with the creation timestamp. Snapshots are sorted by creation date in descending order by default (newest first).

Related operations include GET /wishlist to view current wishlist items and GET /wishlist-item-snapshots/{snapshotId} to retrieve a specific snapshot's detailed information.

requestBody.description: Search criteria, pagination, and sorting parameters for wishlist item snapshots

responseBody.description: Paginated list of wishlist item snapshot summaries

operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Retrieve a single wishlist item snapshot by its UUID identifier from the shopping_mall_wishlist_item_snapshots table.

Implementation steps:
1. Validate the snapshotId parameter is a valid UUID format
2. Verify the authenticated customer has access to this snapshot (ownership check through shopping_mall_wishlist_item_id)
3. Query the shopping_mall_wishlist_item_snapshots table for the record with matching id
4. Join with shopping_mall_wishlist_items to verify customer ownership
5. Return the complete snapshot record including snapshot_data and created_at fields

Validation rules:
- snapshotId must be a valid UUID
- Customer must be authenticated
- Customer must own the wishlist item referenced by the snapshot
- Return 404 if snapshot not found
- Return 403 if customer doesn't own the snapshot

The snapshot_data field contains a complete JSON representation of the wishlist item state at the time of capture, including customer_id, product_id, and created_at timestamp.
operations.description:
Retrieve a specific wishlist item snapshot by its unique identifier.

This operation returns the complete details of a single wishlist item snapshot, which represents an immutable point-in-time capture of a wishlist item's state. Snapshots are used for audit compliance, data recovery, and historical reference purposes.

The snapshot contains the complete state of the wishlist item at the moment it was captured, including the customer reference, product reference, and creation timestamp. This data is stored as JSON in the snapshot_data field and is never modified after creation.

Access to this endpoint requires customer authentication. Customers can only view snapshots of their own wishlist items. The system validates ownership by checking the relationship between the snapshot, the wishlist item, and the authenticated customer's profile.

This operation is typically used for:
- Viewing historical wishlist item states
- Audit trail verification
- Data recovery and dispute resolution
- Understanding when wishlist items were added or modified

parameters.name: snapshotId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the wishlist item snapshot to retrieve

responseBody.description: Complete wishlist item snapshot details

operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_cart_items table for the authenticated customer's cart items.

1. Authenticate the customer from the JWT token and extract customerId.
2. Apply filters from request body:
   - Pagination: page (default 1), limit (default 20, max 100)
   - Sorting: sortBy (created_at, updated_at, quantity), sortOrder (asc, desc)
   - Optional filters: variantId (specific product variant), minQuantity, maxQuantity
3. Filter WHERE conditions:
   - shopping_mall_customer_id = authenticated customerId
   - deleted_at IS NULL (only active cart items)
4. JOIN with shopping_mall_product_variants to get variant details (skuCode, optionValues, priceOverride, stockQuantity)
5. JOIN with shopping_mall_products to get product details (name, basePrice)
6. JOIN with shopping_mall_sellers to get seller information (shopName)
7. Apply ORDER BY based on sortBy and sortOrder parameters
8. Apply OFFSET and LIMIT based on pagination
9. Calculate total count for pagination metadata
10. Return paginated response with cart item summaries and pagination info

Business rules:
- Only return active cart items (deleted_at IS NULL)
- Include stock availability from product variants
- Calculate subtotal for each item (quantity * price)
- Ensure data isolation: customers can only see their own cart items
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of shopping cart items for the authenticated customer.

This operation provides comprehensive access to a customer's shopping cart, allowing them to view all items currently in their cart with detailed product information. The cart items include product variants with quantities, pricing information, and stock availability status.

The response includes each cart item's details such as the product name, variant specifications (SKU code, option values), quantity in cart, unit price, subtotal, and current stock availability. This enables customers to review their cart contents, check item availability, and make informed decisions before checkout.

Supports advanced filtering and sorting capabilities including pagination with configurable page sizes, sorting by various criteria (creation date, update date, quantity), and optional filtering by specific product variants or quantity ranges. The operation automatically excludes soft-deleted cart items, showing only active items in the cart.

This endpoint is commonly used together with other cart operations such as adding items (POST /cart-items), updating quantities (PUT /cart-items/{variantId}), and removing items (DELETE /cart-items/{variantId}). Before placing an order, customers typically review their cart using this operation to verify items and quantities.

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for cart items

responseBody.description: Paginated list of cart item summaries with product and variant details

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific shopping cart item by its unique identifier.

This operation returns complete cart item details including the associated product variant information, quantity, and timestamps. The cart item must belong to the authenticated customer making the request - cross-customer access is not permitted for security reasons.

The cart item data includes references to the product variant which contains SKU code, option values (such as size, color), price override if applicable, and current stock quantity. This information is essential for customers to review their cart contents before proceeding to checkout.

If the cart item has been soft-deleted (removed from cart), it will not be returned. The system treats soft-deleted cart items as non-existent for retrieval operations. Cart items are automatically removed when the associated product or variant is deleted by the seller, or when the customer places an order containing that item.

Related operations include GET /cart-items to list all cart items for the customer, PUT /cart-items/{cartItemId} to update item quantity, and DELETE /cart-items/{cartItemId} to remove an item from the cart.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the shopping_mall_cart_items table for a record matching the provided cartItemId.

Verify that the shopping_mall_customer_id field matches the authenticated customer's ID from the JWT token. Return 403 Forbidden if ownership verification fails.

Check that deleted_at is NULL to ensure the cart item has not been soft-deleted. Return 404 Not Found if deleted or if no matching record exists.

Join with shopping_mall_product_variants to retrieve variant details (sku_code, option_values, price_override, stock_quantity).

Join with shopping_mall_products to retrieve product information (name, description, base_price, category_id).

Optionally join with shopping_mall_product_images to include product thumbnail images in the response.

Return 404 Not Found if the product or variant has been deleted (deleted_at is not NULL).

Include calculated subtotal (price × quantity) in the response.

Use the price_override from variant if present, otherwise use base_price from product.

Ensure transaction isolation to prevent race conditions with concurrent cart modifications.

responseBody.description: Detailed cart item information with product and variant data

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the shopping cart item to retrieve (global scope)
parameters.name: cartItemId

operations.description:
Add a product variant to the customer's shopping cart or update the quantity if the variant already exists in the cart.

This operation allows authenticated customers to add items to their shopping cart for later purchase. When a customer adds a product variant that is already in their cart, the system combines the quantities rather than creating duplicate entries. The cart item includes the product variant's current price, which is captured at the time of addition.

The cart item is associated with the authenticated customer's account and persists until the customer completes checkout or removes the item. Cart items are stored in the shopping_mall_cart_items table with soft-delete capability, allowing for potential audit trail through shopping_mall_cart_snapshots.

Security: Only authenticated customers can add items to their own cart. The system validates that the customer has proper authentication credentials via JWT token in the Authorization header. Each customer can only modify their own cart items.

Related operations: GET /customers/me/cart retrieves all cart items, PUT /customers/me/cart-items/:variantId updates quantity, DELETE /customers/me/cart-items/:variantId removes an item.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Query the shopping_mall_cart_items table to check if a cart item already exists for the given customer and variant combination. If it exists, update the quantity by adding the new quantity to the existing quantity and update the updated_at timestamp. If it doesn't exist, create a new cart item record with the customer's ID, variant ID, and provided quantity.

Before creating or updating, validate that:
1. The customer is authenticated via JWT token
2. The variant exists and is not deleted
3. The variant has sufficient stock quantity for the requested amount
4. The quantity is a positive integer

If the variant is out of stock or deleted, reject the operation with appropriate error code.

On success, return the created or updated cart item with full details including product name, variant options, price, and subtotal calculation.

The operation should be idempotent - if the same request is submitted multiple times with identical parameters, it should return the same result without creating duplicate entries.

responseBody.description: Created or updated cart item with product details

requestBody.description: Product variant and quantity to add to cart

operations.description:
Update the quantity of an existing cart item for the authenticated customer.

This operation allows customers to modify the quantity of a product variant in their shopping cart. When the quantity is updated, the system recalculates the item subtotal and the overall cart total. The cart item's updated_at timestamp is automatically refreshed to reflect the modification.

**Business Rules**: The new quantity must be a positive integer. The system validates that the product variant is still in stock and hasn't been deleted by the seller. If the variant is out of stock or deleted, the update operation fails with an appropriate error message. When updating quantity, the system preserves the original created_at timestamp while updating the updated_at timestamp.

**Related Operations**: Use `GET /cart-items` to list all cart items before updating. Use `POST /cart-items` to add new items to the cart. Use `DELETE /cart-items/{cartItemId}` to remove items from the cart. After updating cart items, the cart is automatically recalculated.

**Idempotency**: This operation supports idempotent retries. If the same update request is sent multiple times with identical parameters, the system returns the same result without creating duplicate modifications.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
1. Extract cartItemId from path parameter and validate UUID format.
2. Authenticate the request and extract the customer ID from the JWT token.
3. Query the shopping_mall_cart_items table for the cart item by ID.
4. Verify ownership: ensure the cart item's shopping_mall_customer_id matches the authenticated customer's ID.
5. Validate that the cart item hasn't been soft-deleted (deleted_at is null).
6. Extract the new quantity from the request body and validate it's a positive integer.
7. Join with shopping_mall_product_variants to check stock availability and verify the variant hasn't been deleted.
8. If stock is insufficient or variant is deleted, return an error response.
9. Update the cart item's quantity and updated_at timestamp in a database transaction.
10. Return the updated cart item with full details including product and variant information.
11. Handle concurrent updates using optimistic locking to prevent race conditions.
12. Support idempotency by checking if the new quantity equals the current quantity and returning early if no change needed.

responseBody.description: Updated cart item with product and variant details

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the cart item to update
parameters.name: cartItemId

requestBody.description: New quantity for the cart item

prerequisites.description: Cart item must be created before it can be updated. The cart item referenced by cartItemId must exist in the shopping_mall_cart_items table and belong to the authenticated customer.

operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Verify the requesting customer owns the cart item by checking shopping_mall_customer_id matches the authenticated customer's ID.

Perform soft deletion by setting deleted_at column to current timestamp on the shopping_mall_cart_items record.

Do not physically delete the record to maintain audit trail in shopping_mall_cart_snapshots.

After deletion, recalculate the customer's cart total by summing remaining active cart items.

If this was the last cart item, the cart becomes empty but the customer can still add new items.

Return 204 No Content on successful deletion.

Return 404 Not Found if cart item does not exist or already deleted.

Return 403 Forbidden if customer attempts to delete another customer's cart item.

No transaction required as this is a single record update operation.
operations.description:
Remove a specific item from the customer's shopping cart.

This operation deletes a cart item identified by its unique cart item ID from the customer's active shopping cart. The cart item is soft-deleted by setting a deletion timestamp, which preserves the record in the database for audit purposes while removing it from the active cart view.

When a cart item is removed, the system automatically recalculates the total price of the remaining cart items. If all cart items are removed, the cart displays an empty state but the customer can continue browsing and adding new products.

Authorization is enforced at the customer level - only the customer who owns the cart item can remove it. The system validates that the authenticated customer's ID matches the shopping_mall_customer_id field in the shopping_mall_cart_items table before allowing deletion.

This operation does not require confirmation from the customer. Cart item removal is immediate and the item is no longer available for checkout once deleted. Historical cart states are preserved in the shopping_mall_cart_snapshots table for data integrity and dispute resolution.

Related operations include GET /cart-items to view all cart items, POST /cart-items to add items, and PUT /cart-items/{cartItemId} to update item quantities.

parameters.name: cartItemId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the cart item to remove from the shopping cart (global scope)

operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_cart_snapshots table filtered by shopping_mall_cart_item_id from path parameter.

Apply pagination from request body (page, limit with default 20, max 100).

Support filtering by:
- created_at date range (from, to)
- quantity range (min, max)

Join with shopping_mall_customers to verify current customer owns the cart item.

Sort by created_at descending (newest snapshots first).

Return paginated results with metadata (total, page, limit, totalPages).

Validate cartItemId exists and belongs to authenticated customer.

Return 404 if cart item not found, 403 if customer doesn't own cart item.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of cart item snapshots for a specific shopping cart item.

This operation provides access to the immutable audit trail of cart item state changes. Each snapshot captures the complete state of a cart item at a specific point in time, including customer ownership, product variant information (SKU code, option values like size and color), price at snapshot time, and quantity. These snapshots are automatically created by the system when cart items are modified or removed.

Snapshots enable historical analysis of customer shopping behavior, audit trail verification, and dispute resolution by showing exactly what was in the cart at any given time. The snapshots remain accessible even after the original cart item is deleted, preserving the complete audit history.

Access is restricted to the customer who owns the cart item. The response includes pagination metadata for efficient browsing of snapshot history. Results are sorted by creation timestamp with newest snapshots first.

Related operations:
- `GET /cart-items/{cartItemId}` - Get current cart item details
- `PATCH /cart-items` - List all cart items for current customer

parameters.name: cartItemId
parameters.description: UUID of the cart item to retrieve snapshots for (global scope)

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for cart item snapshots

responseBody.description: Paginated list of cart item snapshot summaries

operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the shopping_mall_cart_snapshots table for a single record matching both cartItemId and snapshotId.

Implementation steps:
1. Validate both cartItemId and snapshotId are valid UUIDs
2. Query shopping_mall_cart_snapshots WHERE id = snapshotId AND shopping_mall_cart_item_id = cartItemId
3. Verify the snapshot belongs to the requested cart item (security check)
4. Return the snapshot record with all denormalized fields
5. Handle case where snapshot not found (404 error)
6. Handle case where snapshot exists but doesn't match cartItemId (404 error)

No joins needed as all data is denormalized in the snapshot table.

Authorization: Customer can view snapshots of their own cart items. Admin can view any snapshot.
operations.description:
Retrieve a specific shopping cart item snapshot by cart item ID and snapshot ID.

This operation provides access to immutable audit trail snapshots that capture the exact state of a cart item at a specific point in time. Each snapshot contains denormalized data including the customer ownership, product variant SKU code, option values (such as size and color), price at the time of snapshot, and quantity. These snapshots are stored in the shopping_mall_cart_snapshots table, which preserves historical cart states for audit purposes.

Snapshots are automatically created when cart items are modified or deleted, preserving historical state for audit purposes, dispute resolution, and recovery of accidentally deleted cart items. The denormalized structure ensures the snapshot remains accurate even if the original cart item, customer profile, or product data is later modified or deleted. This follows the snapshot pattern used throughout the shopping mall system for data integrity.

Security: Customers can only view snapshots of their own cart items. The system validates that the requesting customer owns the cart item referenced in the snapshot. Administrators have unrestricted access to view all snapshots across the system for audit and support purposes.

Related operations: Use GET /shoppingMall/customer/cart-items/{cartItemId} to retrieve the current cart item state, or PATCH /shoppingMall/customer/cart-items to list all cart items for a customer before accessing specific snapshots.

parameters.name: cartItemId
parameters.description: UUID of the shopping cart item whose snapshot is being retrieved

parameters.name: snapshotId
parameters.description: UUID of the specific cart snapshot to retrieve

responseBody.description: Cart snapshot with denormalized state data

prerequisites.description: Cart item must exist before a snapshot can be created for it. The snapshot captures the state of a specific cart item at a point in time.

operations.description:
Create a new order from the authenticated customer's shopping cart and place it for fulfillment.

This operation converts cart items into a confirmed order, capturing the complete purchase state at the time of order placement. The system creates order records in the shopping_mall_orders table and corresponding order items in the shopping_mall_order_items table. Each order item preserves snapshots of the product, variant, and seller profile at the time of purchase to ensure historical accuracy even if these entities are later modified or deleted.

The shipping address is stored as a JSON snapshot (shipping_address_snapshot field) rather than a foreign key reference. This design ensures that the exact delivery address at order time is preserved indefinitely, even if the customer later modifies, deletes, or updates their saved addresses. The order's total price is also captured as a snapshot and will not change even if product prices are modified after order placement.

Order creation is idempotent to prevent duplicate orders from retry attempts. The system assigns unique idempotency keys based on customer ID, cart contents, and shipping address. If the same order is submitted multiple times with identical parameters, the system returns the original order without creating duplicates. Orders are only created after successful payment confirmation.

After order creation, all cart items included in the order are cleared from the customer's active cart. The order status is initially set to 'paid' and will transition through 'shipped' and 'delivered' states as sellers process and ship the order items. Customers can view their complete order history, and orders are preserved indefinitely even after account deletion for legal and seller record purposes.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
1. Validate the authenticated customer exists and has active status (not suspended or banned).

2. Retrieve cart items from shopping_mall_cart_items table for the authenticated customer where deleted_at is NULL.

3. Validate that all referenced cart items exist and have valid quantities (positive integers).

4. For each cart item, retrieve the associated product variant and verify stock availability (stockQuantity >= requested quantity).

5. Retrieve the shipping address from the customer's addresses table and create a JSON snapshot containing all address fields (recipientName, phoneNumber, streetAddress, city, stateProvince, postalCode, country).

6. Calculate total price by summing (unit price × quantity) for all order items. Use the variant's price or product's basePrice if no override exists.

7. Begin database transaction:
   a. Create order record in shopping_mall_orders with customer_id, shipping_address_snapshot (JSON), total_price, status='paid', and timestamps.
   b. For each cart item, create order item in shopping_mall_order_items with:
      - order_id (newly created order)
      - seller_id (from product variant)
      - quantity, price (snapshot at order time)
      - product_snapshot (JSON of product state)
      - variant_snapshot (JSON of variant state including SKU and option values)
      - seller_profile_snapshot (JSON of seller shop name and description)
      - status='paid'
   c. For each order item, create inventory record in shopping_mall_inventory_records with negative quantity change and reason='order_placement'.
   d. Update cart items by setting deleted_at to current timestamp (soft delete).
   e. Commit transaction.

8. Handle idempotency: Generate idempotency key from customer_id, cart item IDs, and shipping address hash. Store key with order_id for 24 hours. If duplicate request detected, return existing order.

9. Return created order with all order items and their details.

10. Handle errors: If any validation fails or transaction cannot complete, rollback and return appropriate error code (PRODUCT_002 for out of stock, VALIDATION_001 for invalid input, etc.).

responseBody.description: Created order with all order items and details

requestBody.description: Order creation data including cart items, shipping address, and payment confirmation

operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_order_items table with pagination and filtering support.

1. AUTHENTICATION & DATA ISOLATION:
   - Customer context: Filter by shopping_mall_customer_id via order relationship
   - Seller context: Filter by shopping_mall_seller_id directly
   - Admin context: No filtering by actor, return all items
   - Apply soft delete filter: deleted_at IS NULL

2. SEARCH FILTERS (from IShoppingMallOrderItem.IRequest):
   - status: Filter by order item status (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded)
   - orderId: Filter by specific order ID
   - productId: Filter by product ID (requires join)
   - variantId: Filter by variant ID (requires join)
   - createdAtFrom/createdAtTo: Date range filter on created_at
   - priceMin/priceMax: Price range filter
   - quantityMin/quantityMax: Quantity range filter

3. PAGINATION:
   - Accept page (default 1) and limit (default 20, max 100)
   - Return total count for pagination metadata
   - Support cursor-based pagination for large result sets

4. SORTING:
   - Default: created_at DESC (newest first)
   - Support: created_at, updated_at, price, quantity
   - Direction: ASC or DESC

5. JOIN OPERATIONS:
   - Join with shopping_mall_orders for customer_id access
   - Join with shopping_mall_products via product_snapshot parsing (if productId filter used)
   - Join with shopping_mall_product_variants via variant_snapshot parsing (if variantId filter used)

6. RESPONSE CONSTRUCTION:
   - Return IShoppingMallOrderItem.ISummary for each item
   - Include: id, orderId, status, quantity, price, createdAt, productSnapshot (parsed), variantSnapshot (parsed)
   - Exclude sensitive data based on actor type
   - Parse JSON snapshots for product/variant/seller information

7. ERROR HANDLING:
   - Return 404 if no items match criteria
   - Return 403 if actor lacks permission to view items
   - Validate pagination parameters (page >= 1, limit 1-100)
   - Validate status enum values
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of order items from the shopping mall platform.

This operation provides comprehensive search capabilities for order items, allowing users to filter by status, date ranges, price ranges, and specific order or product identifiers. The endpoint supports multiple actor types with appropriate data isolation: customers can view their own order items, sellers can view items containing their products, and administrators can view all order items across the platform.

Order items represent individual line items within customer orders, each capturing a specific purchase with quantity, price at time of purchase, and current fulfillment status. The status field indicates the item's position in the fulfillment workflow: paid (order placed), shipped (item dispatched), delivered (item received), cancelled (pre-shipment cancellation approved), or refunded (post-delivery return approved).

The response includes product and variant snapshots that preserve the state of these entities at order placement time, ensuring historical accuracy even if products or variants are later modified or deleted. Each order item is an independent entity that can be individually shipped, cancelled, refunded, or reviewed.

For customers, this endpoint is useful for viewing purchase history and tracking order status. For sellers, it enables order management and fulfillment tracking. For administrators, it provides oversight of all platform transactions. Related operations include GET /orders/:orderId for detailed order information and POST /shipments for creating shipments for order items.

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for order items

responseBody.description: Paginated list of order item summaries

operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the shopping_mall_order_items table for a single record by primary key (id = itemId).

Authorization Logic:
1. If customer: verify shopping_mall_order_id belongs to the authenticated customer's orders
2. If seller: verify shopping_mall_seller_id matches the authenticated seller
3. If admin: allow access to any order item
4. Return 404 if item not found or access denied

Database Query:
- SELECT * FROM shopping_mall_order_items WHERE id = ? AND deleted_at IS NULL
- Join with shopping_mall_orders to verify customer ownership if needed
- Return single record or null if not found

Data Transformation:
- Parse JSON snapshot fields (product_snapshot, variant_snapshot, seller_profile_snapshot)
- Include all fields: id, orderId, sellerId, quantity, price, status, snapshots, timestamps
- Handle soft-deleted items (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) - return 404

Error Handling:
- 404 Not Found: item doesn't exist or is soft-deleted
- 403 Forbidden: authenticated user lacks permission to view this item
- 401 Unauthorized: missing or invalid authentication token
operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information for a specific order item by its unique identifier.

This operation returns complete order item details including the product and variant information at the time of purchase, seller profile snapshot, quantity ordered, unit price, current fulfillment status, and creation/update timestamps. The order item represents a single line item within a customer's order transaction.

Order items capture the state of products and sellers at purchase time through JSON snapshots, ensuring historical accuracy even if products are later modified or deleted. The status field indicates the current fulfillment state: paid (order placed), shipped (dispatched), delivered (received), cancelled (pre-shipment cancellation approved), or refunded (post-delivery return approved).

Access Control:
- Customers can view order items from their own orders
- Sellers can view order items containing their products
- Administrators can view all order items across the platform
- Soft-deleted order items are not accessible

Related Operations:
- GET /orders/{orderId} - Retrieve the parent order containing this item
- GET /shipments/{shipmentId} - View shipment details if item has been shipped
- POST /orders/items/{itemId}/cancel - Request cancellation (if status is 'paid')
- POST /orders/items/{itemId}/refund - Request refund (if status is 'delivered')
- POST /products/{productId}/reviews - Create a review (if status is 'delivered')

parameters.name: itemId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the order item to retrieve

responseBody.description: Detailed order item information with snapshots

prerequisites.description: Order must be created before order items can exist. Order items are created during checkout when a customer places an order from their cart. The order item references orderId which must exist in the shopping_mall_orders table.

operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_shipments table with pagination and filtering.

1. Authentication: Extract seller_id from authenticated seller session token.

2. Apply seller isolation: Filter shipments by seller_id to ensure sellers only see their own shipments.

3. Apply search filters from request body:
   - status: Filter by delivery_confirmed (true/false) or delivered_at (null/not null)
   - tracking_carrier: Partial match on tracking_carrier field
   - tracking_number: Exact or partial match on tracking_number
   - shipped_at_from: Filter shipments shipped after this date
   - shipped_at_to: Filter shipments shipped before this date
   - delivered_at_from: Filter shipments delivered after this date
   - delivered_at_to: Filter shipments delivered before this date

4. Apply pagination: Use cursor-based or offset-based pagination with page and limit parameters.

5. Apply sorting: Default by created_at descending (newest first), support sorting by shipped_at, delivered_at.

6. Join with shopping_mall_shipment_items to include item count per shipment.

7. Return paginated results with shipment summaries including: id, tracking_carrier, tracking_number, shipped_at, delivered_at, delivery_confirmed, item_count, created_at.

8. Handle edge cases:
   - Return empty array if no shipments match criteria
   - Return 404 if seller not found or suspended
   - Respect soft deletion (exclude deleted_at is not null)

9. Ensure idempotency: Same search parameters always return same results.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of shipments for the authenticated seller.

This operation provides sellers with comprehensive search capabilities to view and manage their shipment history. Sellers can filter shipments by delivery status, tracking information, shipping dates, and delivery dates. The response includes essential shipment information such as tracking carrier, tracking number, shipment date, delivery confirmation status, and the number of order items included in each shipment.

Security: Only authenticated sellers can access this endpoint, and they can only view shipments they created. The system enforces strict seller isolation to prevent unauthorized access to other sellers' shipment data.

The shipment data is sourced from the shopping_mall_shipments table, which tracks physical delivery of order items to customers. Each shipment can contain multiple order items from the same seller, linked through the shopping_mall_shipment_items junction table. Tracking information including carrier name and tracking number is captured when sellers create shipments.

Related operations:
- POST /shipments - Create a new shipment with tracking information
- GET /shipments/{shipmentId} - Get detailed information about a specific shipment
- POST /shipments/{shipmentId}/confirm-delivery - Confirm delivery for a shipment

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering shipments

responseBody.description: Paginated list of shipment summaries with tracking and delivery information

operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the shopping_mall_shipments table by primary key shipmentId.

Verify authorization: seller can only access shipments where seller_id matches their ID, customer can only access shipments linked to their order items through shopping_mall_shipment_items and shopping_mall_order_items.

Join with shopping_mall_shipment_items to retrieve all order items included in this shipment.

For each order item, join with shopping_mall_order_items to get quantity, price, status, and product/variant/seller snapshots.

Return complete shipment object including: id, tracking_carrier, tracking_number, shipped_at, delivered_at, delivery_confirmed, created_at, updated_at, and nested array of order items with their details.

Handle soft-deleted shipments by excluding them from results (deleted_at IS NULL).

Return 404 if shipment not found or user not authorized to view.
operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information for a specific shipment by its unique identifier.

This operation returns comprehensive shipment details including tracking information (carrier name and tracking number), shipment timestamps (when dispatched and when delivered), delivery confirmation status, and the complete list of order items included in this shipment.

Sellers can view shipments they created to track delivery progress and manage their fulfillment operations. Customers can view shipment details for orders they placed to monitor delivery status and confirm receipt.

The response includes nested order item information showing product details, quantities, prices, and current fulfillment status for each item in the shipment. Tracking information is displayed to enable customers to monitor delivery progress through the carrier's tracking system.

This endpoint requires authentication and authorization verification to ensure users can only access shipments relevant to their role (seller shipments or customer order shipments).

parameters.name: shipmentId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the shipment to retrieve

responseBody.description: Detailed shipment information including tracking details and included order items

operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new shipment record in shopping_mall_shipments table.

1. Authenticate the seller from the request context (seller_id from JWT token).

2. Validate request body:
   - order_item_ids: Non-empty array of order item UUIDs
   - tracking_carrier: Non-empty string (e.g., FedEx, UPS, DHL)
   - tracking_number: Non-empty unique string

3. Verify all order items belong to the authenticated seller:
   - Query shopping_mall_order_items for each order_item_id
   - Check that shopping_mall_seller_id matches the authenticated seller_id
   - If any item belongs to another seller, reject with 403 Forbidden

4. Verify order items are in 'paid' status:
   - Only items with status='paid' can be shipped
   - If any item is not in 'paid' status, reject with 400 Bad Request

5. Create shipment record in shopping_mall_shipments:
   - id: Generate UUID
   - seller_id: Authenticated seller's ID
   - tracking_carrier: From request
   - tracking_number: From request
   - shipped_at: Current timestamp
   - delivered_at: Null
   - delivery_confirmed: False
   - created_at: Current timestamp
   - updated_at: Current timestamp

6. Create junction records in shopping_mall_shipment_items:
   - For each order_item_id, create a record linking shipment to order item
   - Ensure unique constraint on (shopping_mall_shipment_id, shopping_mall_order_item_id)

7. Update order item status:
   - For each order item in the shipment, update status from 'paid' to 'shipped'
   - Update updated_at timestamp

8. Return the created shipment with associated order items.

9. Wrap all database operations in a transaction to ensure atomicity.
operations.description:
Create a new shipment for order items belonging to the authenticated seller.

This operation allows sellers to bundle one or more of their order items into a single shipment with carrier tracking information. When a shipment is created, all included order items are automatically updated to "shipped" status, indicating they have been dispatched for delivery.

The seller must provide the shipping carrier name and tracking number for delivery visibility. The system validates that all selected order items belong to the authenticated seller and are in "paid" status (not yet shipped, cancelled, or refunded). If any order item belongs to another seller or is not in a shippable state, the request is rejected.

Each shipment can contain multiple order items from the same seller, enabling consolidated shipping. Different sellers in the same order must create separate shipments for their respective items. The tracking information provided is associated with all items in the shipment and displayed to customers on their order detail pages.

After successful shipment creation, customers can view tracking information and will be able to confirm delivery once the items arrive. If delivery is not manually confirmed within 14 days, the system automatically marks the shipment as delivered.

requestBody.description: Shipment creation information including order items and tracking details

responseBody.description: Created shipment with associated order items

prerequisites.description: Order must be created first to generate order items that can be included in the shipment. The order creation operation creates order items in 'paid' status, which are then available for the seller to bundle into shipments.

operations.description:
Confirm delivery of a shipment to mark all included order items as delivered and enable post-delivery features.

This operation allows customers to confirm that they have received a shipment. When delivery is confirmed, the system updates the shipment record with the delivery timestamp and sets the delivery_confirmed flag to true. All order items included in this shipment are automatically updated to 'delivered' status, enabling customers to write reviews for those items and starting the 7-day refund window.

Security and authorization: Only the customer who owns the order containing the shipment's order items can confirm delivery. The system validates that the authenticated customer is associated with all order items in the shipment before allowing confirmation. Attempts to confirm delivery for shipments not associated with the customer's orders are rejected.

Business rules and validation: Delivery confirmation is only allowed for shipments where delivery_confirmed is false. Duplicate delivery confirmations for the same shipment are prevented. If any order items in the shipment are already cancelled or refunded, delivery confirmation is still allowed for the remaining items. The system automatically marks shipments as delivered after 14 days if not manually confirmed, but manual confirmation prevents this automatic trigger.

After confirming delivery, customers can write reviews for delivered items and request refunds within the 7-day post-delivery window. Sellers can view delivery confirmation status through their shipment management operations.
operations.name: confirmDelivery
operations.specification:
Validate the authenticated customer has permission to confirm delivery for this shipment:
1. Load the shipment by shipmentId from shopping_mall_shipments table
2. Check that shipment.deleted_at is null (shipment is active)
3. Check that shipment.delivery_confirmed is false (not already confirmed)
4. Load all order items in this shipment via shopping_mall_shipment_items junction table
5. Verify all order items belong to orders owned by the authenticated customer
6. Verify shipment status allows delivery confirmation (items should be in 'shipped' status)

Execute delivery confirmation in a database transaction:
1. Update shopping_mall_shipments: set delivery_confirmed = true, delivered_at = current timestamp
2. Update all associated shopping_mall_order_items: set status = 'delivered'
3. Record audit log entry for delivery confirmation

Return the updated shipment object with delivery confirmation details.

Error handling:
- Return 404 if shipment not found or soft-deleted
- Return 400 if shipment already confirmed (delivery_confirmed = true)
- Return 403 if customer does not own any order items in the shipment
- Return 400 if shipment is not in valid state for delivery confirmation
- Return 500 for database transaction failures

parameters.name: shipmentId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the shipment to confirm delivery for

responseBody.description: Updated shipment with delivery confirmation details

prerequisites.description: Order must be created before shipments can be created for its order items. The order contains the order items that will be included in the shipment being confirmed.
Shipment must be created by the seller before delivery can be confirmed. The shipment contains the order items and tracking information that the customer will confirm as delivered.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of order items included in a specific shipment.

This operation returns all order items that are part of the specified shipment by querying the shipment items junction table and joining with the order items table. Each shipment can contain multiple order items from the same seller, consolidated for delivery tracking purposes.

The response includes comprehensive order item information such as product snapshots, variant details, seller profile information, quantity, price at time of purchase, and the current status of each item (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded). This enables sellers and administrators to view the complete contents of a shipment and track the fulfillment status of individual order items.

Access is restricted to the seller who created the shipment or administrators with appropriate permissions. The operation uses the `shopping_mall_shipment_items` junction table to identify which order items belong to the shipment, then retrieves full order item details from the `shopping_mall_order_items` table.

Related operations:
- `GET /shoppingMall/seller/shipments/{shipmentId}` retrieves the shipment details including tracking information
- `PATCH /shoppingMall/seller/orderItems` searches order items by various criteria
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the shopping_mall_shipment_items junction table filtered by the provided shipmentId from the path parameter. Join with shopping_mall_order_items to retrieve complete order item details including quantity, price, status, and snapshot data.

Apply pagination parameters from the request body (page, limit) to limit result set size. Default page size is 20, maximum is 100.

Support optional filtering on order item status if provided in the request body (e.g., filter by 'shipped' or 'delivered' items only).

Sort results by created_at in descending order (newest items first) unless a different sort order is specified.

Validate that the shipment exists and is not soft-deleted. Return 404 if shipment not found.

Verify authorization: only the seller who created the shipment or administrators can access this endpoint. Deny access for other users with 403.

Return paginated response with total count, current page, page size, and array of order item summaries.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of order items included in the shipment

parameters.name: shipmentId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the shipment to retrieve items for

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for order items in the shipment

prerequisites.description: Shipment must be created before its order items can be retrieved. The shipmentId path parameter requires an existing shipment record in shopping_mall_shipments table.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of order items included in a specific shipment.

This operation returns all order items that are part of the specified shipment, including product details, quantity, price at time of purchase, and current fulfillment status. Each shipment can contain multiple order items from the same seller, consolidated for delivery tracking purposes.

The response includes comprehensive order item information such as product snapshots, variant details, seller profile information, and the current status of each item (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded). This enables sellers and administrators to view the complete contents of a shipment and track the fulfillment status of individual items.

Access is restricted to the seller who created the shipment or administrators with appropriate permissions. Customers can view shipment items through their order detail pages, which provides a customer-specific view of their purchases.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the shopping_mall_shipment_items junction table filtered by the provided shipmentId from the path parameter. Join with shopping_mall_order_items to retrieve complete order item details including quantity, price, status, and snapshot data.

This operation provides comprehensive search capabilities for browsing customer reviews. Reviews are customer feedback on purchased products, containing star ratings (1-5) and optional text content describing the purchase experience. The system ensures only non-deleted reviews are returned, maintaining data integrity while respecting customer deletion requests.

Reviews are sorted by submission date in descending order (newest first) by default, helping customers see the most recent feedback. Each review is associated with a specific order item, ensuring customers can only review products they have actually purchased and received.

The operation supports multiple filtering options including product ID, customer ID, rating value, and creation date range. This enables targeted searches such as finding all reviews for a specific product, viewing a customer's review history, or finding highly-rated products.

When a review is from a deleted customer account, the system displays the reviewer as "deleted user" while preserving the review content for other customers' reference. This maintains the integrity of product feedback even when customer accounts are removed.

Related operations include creating new reviews (POST /products/{productId}/reviews), updating existing reviews (PUT /reviews/{reviewId}), and deleting reviews (DELETE /reviews/{reviewId}).

3. Verify the authenticated customer's ID matches the review's shopping_customer_id field. If not the same, return 403 Forbidden error - customers can only view their own review details.

4. Join with shopping_mall_order_items to verify the review is associated with a valid order item.

5. Return the review object with all fields: id, shopping_order_item_id, shopping_customer_id, rating, content, created_at, updated_at.

6. If no review found or review is deleted, return 404 Not Found error.

7. If customer is not the owner, return 403 Forbidden error.

Access to review details is restricted to the review owner only. Customers cannot view other customers' review details to protect privacy and prevent unauthorized access to personal feedback. The system verifies that the authenticated customer matches the review's author before returning any data.

Reviews that have been soft-deleted are not accessible through this endpoint. If a customer has deleted their review, attempting to retrieve it will result in a 404 Not Found error. The system maintains immutable snapshots of deleted reviews for audit purposes, but these are not exposed through the customer-facing API.

This operation is typically used when a customer wants to review their own feedback before making edits, or to verify the content of their submitted review. It can be used in conjunction with the update and delete review operations to manage review lifecycle.

operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Service layer implementation for creating a new product review.

1. AUTHENTICATION: Verify the requester is an authenticated customer via JWT token.

2. VALIDATION: Validate the request body contains valid data:
   - orderItemId must be a valid UUID
   - rating must be an integer between 1 and 5 (inclusive)
   - content is optional, if provided must be non-empty string

3. ORDER ITEM VERIFICATION: Query shopping_mall_order_items table for the specified orderItemId:
   - Verify the order item exists and is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null)
   - Verify the order item's status is 'delivered' (customers can only review received items)
   - Verify the order item belongs to the authenticated customer (via shopping_mall_order_id -> shopping_mall_orders -> shopping_mall_customer_id)

4. EXISTING REVIEW CHECK: Query shopping_mall_reviews table to ensure no existing review exists for this orderItemId (enforce @@unique constraint on shopping_order_item_id).

5. REVIEW CREATION: Insert new record into shopping_mall_reviews table:
   - id: Generate new UUID
   - shopping_order_item_id: From request
   - shopping_customer_id: From authenticated user session
   - rating: From request (1-5)
   - content: From request (nullable)
   - created_at: Current timestamp
   - updated_at: Current timestamp
   - deleted_at: null (active review)

6. RESPONSE: Return the created review object with all fields including generated id and timestamps.

7. ERROR HANDLING:
   - Return 401 if customer not authenticated
   - Return 404 if order item not found
   - Return 403 if order item does not belong to customer or status is not 'delivered'
   - Return 409 if review already exists for this order item
   - Return 400 for invalid rating range or malformed request
operations.description:
Create a new product review for a purchased and delivered order item.

This operation allows authenticated customers to write reviews for products they have purchased and received. Reviews are essential for helping other buyers make informed purchasing decisions and provide valuable feedback to sellers.

Each review is associated with a specific order item, ensuring that only customers who have actually purchased and received the product can write reviews. The system enforces that the order item status must be 'delivered' before allowing review creation, preventing premature reviews on items still in transit or not yet shipped.

Reviews consist of a required star rating (1-5 stars) and optional text content describing the customer's experience with the product. The rating helps provide quick visual feedback, while the text content allows customers to share detailed insights about product quality, value, and suitability.

The system maintains a one-review-per-order-item constraint, meaning each customer can only write one review for a specific order item. If a customer wants to modify their review, they must use the update operation rather than creating a new one. Reviews support soft deletion, allowing customers to remove their feedback while preserving the data for administrative purposes.

When a customer's account is deleted, their reviews are preserved and displayed with the reviewer identified as "deleted user" to maintain the integrity of product feedback while respecting privacy requirements. Review snapshots are automatically created when reviews are modified, providing an audit trail for dispute resolution.

responseBody.description: Created review with all fields including generated ID and timestamps
